summary: This paper, from the Proceedings of the XI Scientific Meeting of the Spanish Astronomical Society (Teruel, 2014), introduces MIARMA, a gap-filling method for astronomical time series that uses local ARMA models with forward-backward prediction to preserve the frequency content of the signal. The authors argue that linear interpolation, commonly used on CoRoT data, biases power spectra with orbital aliases, while MIARMA removes these effects. They test the method on three CoRoT stars: the delta Scuti star HD 174966, the Be star HD 51193, and the solar-like star HD 49933. The method was accepted by the CoRoT Scientific Committee for implementation in the next data correction.
one_line: MIARMA is an ARMA-based gap-filling method that preserves the frequency content of CoRoT stellar light curves better than linear interpolation.
key_facts: MIARMA stands for Method of Interpolation by Autoregressive and Moving Average and was introduced by J. Pascual-Granado, R. Garrido, and J. C. Suárez.
The paper was presented at the XI Scientific Meeting of the Spanish Astronomical Society held September 8–12, 2014, in Teruel, Spain.
MIARMA selects the ARMA model order using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC).
The method fits local ARMA models to the data segments before and after each gap and interpolates the gap with a weighted forward and backward prediction.
The abstract states that MIARMA can recover signal that no analytic interpolation method can.
The method was accepted by the CoRoT Scientific Committee for implementation in the next correction of the data.
Wold's theorem is cited as the basis for representing any stationary signal as a deterministic (AR) plus stochastic (MA) process.

For HD 174966, a delta Scuti star, the paper reports that linear interpolation leaves the power spectrum seriously affected by the CoRoT spectral window, while ARMA interpolation eliminates these effects.
For HD 51193, a Be star, the power spectrum from linearly interpolated data is clearly biased by the CoRoT orbital frequency of 13.97 cycles per day.
The solar-like star HD 49933 has gaps of most frequent length 9 minutes, with some gaps lasting up to 0.2 days, and very high noise.
For HD 49933, the paper finds non-negligible and non-systematic amplitude differences between ARMA and linear interpolation spectra.
The passing of the South Atlantic Anomaly (SAA) introduces most of the invalid data gaps in CoRoT observations.
The work was supported by project AYA2012-39346-C02-01 of the Plan Nacional de Investigación in Spain.
The authors are affiliated with the Instituto de Astrofísica de Andalucía (CSIC) and the University of Granada.
